MEASUREMENT CORRECTION — a -run-filtered run cannot reproduce this class of flake, and two of the
three measurements on this investigation were filtered.

Measured 2026-08-02, /tmp/dk-flake at 353c41e9, load average ~98 (14 busy loops on 18 cores):

  scripts/test.sh -race -count=20 -run "TestOwnedCloseDrains...|...DoesNotPin...|TestConsumerCLIScope..." .
  UNFIXED: 0 failures / 60 executions
  FIXED:   0 failures / 60 executions

Neither arm went red, so the run distinguishes nothing. The earlier "0/60 idle" figure has the
same defect and should not be cited as evidence of anything.

Why filtering defeats it: go test runs the tests within one package sequentially, so -run over
three tests in the root package leaves the machine running one test binary. The observations that
DID catch the bug were full-suite (./...) runs, where every package binary runs in parallel and
each spawns its own children — the refuter hit it in 2 of 3 full-suite runs, and the original
sighting was also full-suite. The contention that widens the zombie window comes from the OTHER
packages, which a filtered run excludes by construction.

Synthetic CPU load is not a substitute. Busy loops raise load average without creating the
fork/reap pressure that the sibling test binaries create; the arm above ran at load ~98 and still
saw nothing.

Rule for this suite: reproduce and prove flakes with `scripts/test.sh -race -count=1 ./...`
repeated N times, never with -run. A targeted run is for iterating on a fix, never for judging
whether the fix worked.

This repeats a mistake already recorded once this phase — a lane measured with --filter and
declared a bug unreproducible while the artifacts proving it sat in a sibling directory. Same
shape, different lane.
